video_caption: The video opens with a close-up of a blurred "CC" (Creative Commons) logo, which then clarifies into the distinct circular "CC" symbol. This transitions to a black screen displaying "Attribution" with a stylized person icon and "CC BY" below it. Following this, a black screen shows "Kelsey Merkley" and "Horizontal Hostility" in white text, introducing the speaker and the topic of the presentation. The scene then reveals a wide shot of a woman with dark hair, wearing a dark blue sleeveless dress and red earrings, standing on a stage behind a black podium with a silver laptop. She is actively speaking and gesturing, addressing an audience whose heads are visible in the foreground. To the left of the stage is a red and white banner displaying the Creative Commons logo. Behind her, a large screen initially shows a bright blue background with the white text "horizontal hostility." She elaborates on this concept, referencing historical examples such as a deaf woman being criticized for speaking rather than signing and a lighter-skinned Black professor being deemed "not Black enough." The screen subsequently changes to a white background with purple text that reads "if you aren't all in, you don't belong here." The video concludes with the screen reverting to a blue background, now displaying the white text "the women's suffrage movement."

A woman with dark hair and red earrings, wearing a dark dress, stands at a podium on a dark stage, speaking into a microphone while occasionally looking at a laptop positioned on the podium. Behind her, a large blue screen displays white text that initially reads "the women's suffrage movement" (the women's suffrage movement). A red banner with the "cc" (Creative Commons) logo is visible to the left of the stage. After a brief close-up of the woman, the text on the blue screen changes to "15th Amendment" (15th Amendment) as she continues her speech.

A woman with dark, wavy hair and distinctive red earrings, dressed in a dark blue, V-neck, sleeveless dress, stands at a dark-colored podium on a stage. She is looking down at a silver laptop with an Apple logo, which rests on the podium, and appears to be reading or referencing it as she speaks into two microphones positioned on either side of the podium. Her expression is focused and serious. Behind her is a large, illuminated blue screen, contrasting with the dark background of the rest of the stage, where some blue objects are visible on a lower stand to her left.

A woman with dark, wavy hair, wearing a dark blue V-neck sleeveless dress and red earrings, stands behind a podium with a laptop on it, looking down as she speaks. A close-up shot shows her with her hands clasped in front of her, then she gestures slightly. The background is a large, bright blue screen. The scene then transitions to a wider shot, revealing the full stage and a partial view of the audience in the foreground. The woman is still at the podium. On the blue screen behind her, the white text "15th Amendment" appears. To the left of the stage, a red banner with a white Creative Commons "cc" logo is visible.

A woman in a black dress stands on a dark stage, presenting to an audience, with a red Creative Commons banner positioned to her left. On a large projector screen behind her, an illustration of "Lucy Stone" is displayed, identified as an "abolitionist + women's rights activist", with "Image by Ron Comics" also visible. The woman gestures with her right hand while speaking. Around 00:05, the screen transitions to a prominent quote by Lucy Stone, enclosed in quotation marks: "I do not know what bloodshed may come by it. All I do know is, that we have no right to keep a Union with slaveholders. Slavery shall be abolished, or the Union shall be dissolved." The woman continues to speak, looking towards the screen.

A woman with dark hair, wearing a dark top, stands behind a black podium on the left side of a dimly lit stage, looking at a laptop and speaking. To her left, a red banner displays the white Creative Commons logo and text. In the background, an audience is seated. A large screen behind her displays presentations. Initially, the screen shows a quote by Lucy Stone on a white background: "I do not know what bloodshed may come by it. All I do know is, that we have no right to keep a Union with slaveholders. Slavery shall be abolished, or the Union shall be dissolved." (The speaker is discussing historical figures who advocated for change). The screen then transitions to a blue title "Audre Lorde" above a stylized, colorful portrait of the author, with a small credit "Image by Jessica Sabogal." (This introduces a new figure the speaker is referencing). Following this, the screen displays another quote on a white background, attributed to Audre Lorde: "It is learning how to take our differences and make them strengths. For the **master's tools** will never dismantle the master's house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about **genuine change**." (The speaker uses this quote to talk about methods of bringing about change). Finally, the screen transitions to a solid blue background with large white text: "The free software and open source movement maybe" (introducing the next topic or question of the presentation).

A woman with dark hair, wearing a dark sleeveless top and pants, stands at a podium on a large stage, giving a presentation to an audience. To her left, a black table holds a laptop, and a tall red banner displays the "cc" Creative Commons logo. Behind her, a large screen features a blue background. From 00:00 to 00:14, the screen shows white text that reads, "The free software and open source movement maybe." At 00:14, the screen changes to display four white icons on the blue background: the open-source logo and a checkmark on the top row, and a beer mug and an 'X' mark on the bottom row.

A woman with dark, shoulder-length hair, wearing a dark sleeveless top and pants, stands on a stage to the left of a podium, gesturing with her right hand while looking at a laptop on the podium. Behind her, a large blue screen initially displays four white icons: the GitHub logo (a circular keyhole shape) and a checkmark in the top row, and a beer mug and an 'X' mark in the bottom row, visually representing concepts often associated with "free as in speech" (open source) versus "free as in beer" (gratis). To the far left of the stage, a tall red banner with the Creative Commons "CC" logo is visible. The audience is seated in the darkened foreground. At 0:06, the screen changes to a solid blue background with white text that reads, "The Masters of Open Source." Subsequently, at 0:16, the screen transitions to a white background displaying a quote in purple text: "...when we saw the success that open source was having, it served as a guiding light to us." Below the quote, also in purple, is the attribution: "- The Budapest Open Access Initiative." The woman continues to speak, occasionally gesturing, as the slides change.

The video opens with a medium shot of a woman speaking on a stage, addressing an unseen audience. She has dark hair and is wearing a dark dress and glasses. She stands behind a black podium with a microphone, occasionally looking down at notes. To her left, a red banner displays the white "CC" logo and "creative commons" text. Behind her, a large white screen shows a quote in purple text: "...when we saw the success that open source was having, it served as a guiding light to us." Below the quote, it reads "- The Budapest Open Access Initiative". The stage is dimly lit, with the woman and banner illuminated. The audience is visible in the foreground as dark silhouettes. At the 0:25 mark, the screen behind her transitions to a solid blue background with white text that reads "what our masters built", while the woman continues to speak, maintaining her position and posture.

In the video segment, a woman with dark, wavy hair, wearing a dark blue or black spaghetti strap dress and red earrings, is speaking into two microphones from behind a dark wooden podium. She looks down at a silver Apple laptop resting on the podium, occasionally gesturing with her hands as she delivers her speech. Behind her, a large, bright blue screen fills the background. She passionately states, "rejected, excluded, and assaulted those who disagreed or were different. Come for the open source, be rewarded with hateful culture, a culture based on Linus, who is feared by as many as those who celebrated him. Python used the terms master and slave. Wikipedia, notorious for its toxic editors and the damage to the community that happens when they are tolerated. This is the culture..." Around the 00:34 mark, the camera zooms out to reveal the full stage and a seated audience. The blue screen behind the speaker now displays a black and white portrait of a woman with short, curly hair and glasses. Text on the screen identifies her as "Christine Peterson" and notes, "Image by Peter Adams Faces of Open Source" (Image by Peter Adams Faces of Open Source). To the left of the stage, an orange banner with the "CC" logo and the text "creative commons" is visible. The stage is brightly lit, while the audience, some holding up phones, is in dimmer lighting.

She is looking down at a silver laptop on the podium and gesturing with her hands. To her left, a red banner displays the Creative Commons "cc" logo and "creative commons" text. Behind her, a large screen shows a black-and-white stylized portrait of a woman with glasses, labeled "Christine Peterson" in blue text. Below the portrait, in white text, it reads "Image by Peter Adams" and "Faces of Open Source." As the woman speaks, the screen abruptly changes to a black background with the white text "traitor*" displayed prominently in the center.

Behind her, a large screen initially displays a blue background with white text that reads "all" (with a caret above the 'a') and "You are welcome here."
